gaps.q: The Edge Console header still renders the static text 'EDGE CONSOLE · COORDINATOR 8004' / 'COORD :8004' (EdgeConsole.tsx:355/358) while every request in this run went to :8006 (trace network log + supplemental observations). Pre-existing and outside this slice, but every screenshot therefore carries a port label that is not runtime truth. Claimed failure mode: a reviewer reading the screenshots could believe the evidence hit the default :8004 deployment coordinator instead of the fresh branch process.

On #a1-workbench the dev-routes note co-occurs with a governance 502. The supplemental capture shows the note persists across a second 502 (retry click) and the code gates it on isCoordinatorNotFound (status===404), but no browser run isolates the two conditions (dev routes enabled + governance 502 → note must be absent); only vitest covers that branch. Claimed failure mode: the note could be shown for a non-404 failure, i.e. a false 'dev routes closed' message.

The user-facing half of T4 (LAN operator triggering a conversion from the UI with an operator token) does not exist in this slice: every T4 observation is a server-side Playwright request; in the browser the conversion trigger path is still allowlist-only (403 for a LAN origin). Claimed failure mode: the slice could be read as 'operator can trigger conversion on canonical-linux' when the UI cannot do it yet (spec §3 defers the /ui token input to another slice).

Rate limiting was observed only as 'the 11th token request on a fresh process → 429 + Retry-After=60'; the spec's loop tolerates any 429 within 11 attempts and nothing observes the window actually expiring (a token request succeeding again after 60 s) or the per-IP keying across sources. Claimed failure mode: a limiter that never resets, or one keyed globally instead of per source IP, would pass this evidence unchanged.

All evidence is from a local branch coordinator with the plan's test-only env; canonical-linux (181) with ENABLE_DEV_ROUTES=false and a non-default DEV_AUTH_TOKEN is owner action and unobserved. tasks.md itself records a deployment-order hazard (setting ENABLE_DEV_ROUTES=false before this frontend PR is deployed makes main's #demo-control show a misleading storage_empty). Claimed failure mode: D3/T4 could be 'green' locally yet not in effect, or in effect with the misleading empty state, on 181.

The rubric's 'runtime ID visible' and 'loading state visible' rows are not observed: the disabled state has no job/session ID by design and the page's pre-fetch text is 'runtime: idle' (not a loading indicator) for the ~200 ms before the 404 lands. Claimed failure mode: an operator opening #demo-control on a slow link sees 'runtime: idle' and an empty fixture list for that interval, which is the same shape as the misleading storage_empty state, before the honest notice appears.

The subject head d2e0805 is one commit behind origin/main (75e9aab #701 landed after the branch's merge-base d5f2d77). Claimed failure mode: if P6 merges main before the PR, the merged tree differs from the evidenced tree (base freshness) and this P4 capture would no longer describe the head being shipped.
